newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia budget bill due in Senate next week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia budget bill due in Senate next week.

text.p: The Australian government said on Thursday that it would return a key budget bill, to limit new migrants' welfare entitlements, to the upper house of parliament, the Senate, next week.
"Social security is on the list but I think you can fairly safely say it won't be up (in the Senate) until next week," a spokesman for government leader in the Senate, Robert Hill, told Reuters.
Under the Social Security (Newly Arrived Residents' Waiting Periods) Bill, 1996, the government wants to exclude migrants from social security payments for two years after arrival.

The bill failed to pass the Senate in its original form late last year and the government estimated the amendments would cost most of the bill's value, according to government estimates - A$130 million in 1997/98 and A$400 million over four years.
"Because of the delay we are now looking at savings of about A$350 million over four years. That's if it's passed," a spokeswoman for Social Security Minister Jocelyn Newman said.
The government has previously said if the bill is rejected for a second time it will be put back to the Senate again three months later.
If it is then rejected it could give the government the constitutional option of an early national election dissolving of both houses of parliament -- a double dissolution.
